note: Every entry was fetched on the date in its 'fetched' field; licence is as stated on the repository, dataset card or arXiv page.

sections.title: Function-level code benchmarks
sections.blurb: Self-contained problems scored by running unit tests on a single generated function or program.

sections.title: Repository-level and issue-resolution benchmarks
sections.blurb: Tasks set inside a real code base: resolve an issue, complete code that depends on other files, or ship a change that passes the project's tests.

sections.title: Agent harnesses and scaffolds
sections.blurb: Open-source agents and the tooling used to run them against the benchmarks above.

sections.title: Training environments and datasets for coding agents
sections.blurb: Executable task collections and agent trajectories released for fine-tuning or reinforcement learning.

sections.title: Terminal and tool-use benchmarks
sections.blurb: Benchmarks where the agent works through a shell, tools or a simulated user rather than returning a single patch.

sections.title: Evaluation methodology and statistics
sections.blurb: How to measure, compare and report results: estimators, error bars, judge behaviour and benchmark design.

sections.title: Contamination and leakage analyses
sections.blurb: Studies of test data leaking into training data or into the task itself, and benchmarks built to limit it.

entries.name: HumanEval
entries.summary: 164 hand-written Python problems, each a function signature and docstring checked by unit tests, with the harness that runs them; its authors now mark it deprecated and unmaintained.

entries.name: MBPP
entries.summary: About 1,000 crowd-sourced entry-level Python problems, each with a task description, a reference solution and three test cases.

entries.name: APPS
entries.summary: Training and evaluation code and a dataset download for APPS, which its paper's arXiv abstract describes as 10,000 coding problems, from one-line solutions to substantial algorithmic challenges.

entries.name: DS-1000
entries.summary: 1,000 data science problems drawn from StackOverflow and spanning seven Python libraries such as NumPy and Pandas, with execution-based checks.

entries.name: EvalPlus (HumanEval+ and MBPP+)
entries.summary: Framework that adds many generated test inputs to HumanEval and MBPP so that plausible but wrong solutions are caught.

entries.name: CRUXEval
entries.summary: 800 short Python functions, each with one input-output pair, used for two tasks: predict the output from the input and predict an input for the output; the repository is archived.

entries.name: LiveCodeBench
entries.summary: Code benchmark that keeps adding problems from programming contests with their release dates, covering generation, self-repair, test output prediction and execution.

entries.name: BigCodeBench
entries.summary: Python tasks that require calls to many functions across common libraries, offered as docstring completion and as natural-language instructions; the repository is archived.

entries.name: SWE-bench
entries.summary: Benchmark and Docker-based evaluation harness in which a system receives a real GitHub issue and its repository and must produce a patch that makes the hidden tests pass.

entries.name: SWE-bench (paper)
entries.summary: Introduces SWE-bench: 2,294 issue and pull request pairs from 12 popular Python repositories, scored by running the repository's tests.

entries.name: SWE-bench Lite
entries.summary: A 300-instance test subset of SWE-bench, issue and pull request pairs from 11 Python repositories checked by unit tests, plus a 23-instance dev split.

entries.name: SWE-bench Verified
entries.summary: A 500-instance subset of the SWE-bench test set whose issues and tests were checked by human annotators.

entries.name: SWE-bench Multimodal
entries.summary: 617 issue-resolution tasks from 17 user-facing JavaScript libraries, each with at least one image in its problem statement or tests.

entries.name: SWE-bench Multilingual
entries.summary: 300 SWE-bench-style issue-resolution tasks from 41 repositories in 9 programming languages.

entries.name: SWE-bench-java
entries.summary: A Java version of the SWE-bench task, with the dataset, a Docker-based evaluation setup and a leaderboard.

entries.name: Multi-SWE-bench
entries.summary: Multilingual issue-resolution benchmark covering languages such as Java, TypeScript, JavaScript, Go, Rust, C and C++, with its evaluation code.

entries.name: SWE-PolyBench
entries.summary: Repository-level, execution-based benchmark of coding tasks in Python, Java, JavaScript and TypeScript, with additional metrics based on syntax tree analysis.

entries.name: SWE-Lancer
entries.summary: Repository for SWE-Lancer, which its paper's arXiv abstract describes as over 1,400 freelance software tasks from Upwork with real payouts; it is archived and points to openai/preparedness, now openai/frontier-evals.

entries.name: SWE-bench-Live
entries.summary: Issue-resolution benchmark refreshed over time from issues created since 2024, built by an automated pipeline that also sets up a Docker image per task.

entries.name: RepoBench
entries.summary: Benchmark for repository-level code completion with three tasks: retrieving relevant cross-file snippets, completing the next line, and both together.

entries.name: CrossCodeEval
entries.summary: Code completion benchmark in four languages where the correct completion depends on context from other files in the repository.

entries.name: REPOCOD
entries.summary: 980 whole-function generation tasks from 11 large Python projects, many needing repository context, each checked by the project's developer-written tests.

entries.name: SWE-agent
entries.summary: Agent that takes a GitHub issue and tries to fix it through a purpose-built agent-computer interface for editing files; its README says mini-swe-agent has superseded it.

entries.name: mini-swe-agent
entries.summary: Agent of about 100 lines of Python whose only tool is bash, from the SWE-agent team, usable as a baseline or a command-line helper.

entries.name: OpenHands
entries.summary: Open platform for software development agents that write code, run commands and browse the web inside a sandbox.

entries.name: Aider
entries.summary: Pair-programming tool that runs in the terminal and edits files in a local git repository through a language model.

entries.name: Agentless
entries.summary: Fixed three-phase pipeline of localisation, repair and patch validation for issue resolution, without letting the model choose its next action.

entries.name: AutoCodeRover
entries.summary: Program-improvement agent that uses code search over the program structure to localise an issue before writing a patch.

entries.name: Moatless Tools
entries.summary: Experimental code-editing tools for large existing code bases, built around putting the right context into the prompt, evaluated on SWE-bench.

entries.name: Codex CLI
entries.summary: Coding agent that runs locally in the terminal.

entries.name: sb-cli
entries.summary: Command-line client for submitting SWE-bench predictions and running the evaluation remotely.

entries.name: SWE-bench experiments
entries.summary: Published predictions, execution logs, trajectories and results from many system submissions to SWE-bench.

entries.name: Harbor
entries.summary: Framework for evaluating and improving agents, pointed to by the Terminal-Bench authors for running Terminal-Bench 2.0.

entries.name: SWE-Gym
entries.summary: Code for training software engineering agents and verifiers on executable Python tasks.

entries.name: SWE-Gym dataset
entries.summary: 2,438 task instances from 11 Python repositories, collected the same way as SWE-bench, each with a runnable environment and unit tests.

entries.name: SWE-smith
entries.summary: Pipeline that builds an execution environment for a Python code base and synthesises many task instances that break its existing tests.

entries.name: SWE-smith dataset
entries.summary: Task instances produced by the SWE-smith pipeline; the card notes it is no longer actively updated.

entries.name: SWE-smith trajectories
entries.summary: 5,017 agent trajectories used to fine-tune a Qwen 2.5 Coder model into the SWE-agent-LM-32B agent.

entries.name: R2E-Gym
entries.summary: Procedurally curated executable environments for training open-weight software agents, plus hybrid verifiers for choosing among candidate patches.

entries.name: SWE-rebench
entries.summary: Large collection of interactive issue-resolution tasks gathered by an automated pipeline, for training and evaluating software agents.

entries.name: SWE-agent trajectories
entries.summary: 80,036 trajectories produced by an agent built on SWE-agent with various models choosing the actions.

entries.name: SWE-RL
entries.summary: Code for reinforcement learning on open-source software history with a rule-based reward from similarity to the developer's actual change.

entries.name: SWE-Gym (paper)
entries.summary: Describes SWE-Gym and reports fine-tuning agents and outcome verifiers on its trajectories.

entries.name: SWE-smith (paper)
entries.summary: Describes the SWE-smith data generation pipeline and the agent model trained on its trajectories.

entries.name: InterCode
entries.summary: Framework for interactive coding with execution feedback, where the model's actions are code run in Bash, SQL or Python environments.

entries.name: AgentBench
entries.summary: Benchmark of eight interactive environments, including operating system and database tasks, for evaluating language models acting as agents.

entries.name: tau-bench
entries.summary: Conversations between an agent with domain tools and policies and a language-model-simulated user, scored by the final database state; its README warns that these tasks are outdated and points to tau2-bench.

entries.name: tau-bench (paper)
entries.summary: Introduces tau-bench and the pass^k metric for how consistently an agent succeeds across repeated trials of the same task.

entries.name: tau2-bench
entries.summary: Repository of τ²-bench, whose cited paper puts agent and simulated user in a dual-control environment, and now of τ-bench 2.0, which adds tasks in six languages in text and full-duplex voice.

entries.name: Terminal-Bench
entries.summary: Tasks for agents working in a real terminal sandbox, such as compiling code or setting up servers, with an execution harness; this repository holds the first version.

entries.name: Evaluating Large Language Models Trained on Code
entries.summary: Introduces Codex and the HumanEval set and reports how solve rates rise when many samples are drawn per problem.

entries.name: Adding Error Bars to Evals
entries.summary: Treats eval questions as a sample from a larger population and gives formulas for standard errors, paired model comparisons and sample size planning.

entries.name: Judging LLM-as-a-Judge with MT-Bench and Chatbot Arena
entries.summary: Studies strong models as judges of open-ended answers and documents position, verbosity and self-enhancement biases alongside agreement with humans.

entries.name: Large Language Models are not Fair Evaluators
entries.summary: Shows that a model judge's preference between two responses can flip when their order is swapped, and proposes calibration strategies.

entries.name: Judging the Judges
entries.summary: Compares thirteen judge models with human scores and finds weaknesses such as leniency and sensitivity to prompt length and complexity.

entries.name: Rigorous Evaluation of Large Language Models for Code Generation
entries.summary: The EvalPlus paper: shows that the small test suites in existing code benchmarks accept wrong solutions, and extends them with generated tests.

entries.name: Establishing Best Practices for Building Rigorous Agentic Benchmarks
entries.summary: Catalogues task setup and reward design flaws in agentic benchmarks and proposes the Agentic Benchmark Checklist (ABC).

entries.name: SWE-agent: Agent-Computer Interfaces Enable Automated Software Engineering
entries.summary: Argues that the interface an agent uses to view and edit code affects its results, and studies interface design choices on SWE-bench.

entries.name: Agentless (paper)
entries.summary: Asks whether complex autonomous agents are needed for issue resolution and compares them with a fixed localise-repair-validate pipeline.

entries.name: SWE-Bench+
entries.summary: Manual review of successful SWE-bench patches that finds solutions leaked in the issue text, tests too weak to reject wrong patches, and most issues predating model knowledge cut-offs.

entries.name: The SWE-Bench Illusion
entries.summary: Probes whether models can name the buggy file path from the issue text alone, as evidence that SWE-bench Verified scores partly reflect memorisation.

entries.name: LiveCodeBench (paper)
entries.summary: Describes LiveCodeBench and uses problem release dates relative to model training cut-offs to show contamination on older problems.

entries.name: Data Contamination Through the Lens of Time
entries.summary: Uses model training cut-offs as a natural experiment on Codeforces and Project Euler problems released over time to find contamination trends.

entries.name: Rethinking Benchmark and Contamination for Language Models with Rephrased Samples
entries.summary: Shows that paraphrased or translated test items pass n-gram decontamination, including for HumanEval, and proposes a model-based decontamination check.

entries.name: Benchmarking Benchmark Leakage in Large Language Models
entries.summary: Detects possible benchmark leakage with perplexity and n-gram accuracy, applied to 31 models on mathematical reasoning benchmarks, and proposes a Benchmark Transparency Card for reporting.

entries.name: SWE-rebench (paper)
entries.summary: Describes the pipeline that collects over 21,000 interactive Python tasks for SWE-rebench and a contamination-free benchmark built from freshly collected tasks.

entries.name: SWE-bench Goes Live!
entries.summary: The SWE-bench-Live paper: argues fixed benchmarks risk overfitting and contamination and presents a continuously updated set of tasks.

entries.name: MultiPL-E
entries.licence: BSD 3-Clause License with Machine Learning Restriction
entries.summary: System that translates unit-test-driven Python benchmarks to other languages, used to port HumanEval and MBPP to 18 further programming languages.

entries.name: ClassEval
entries.summary: 100 hand-built class-level Python tasks with 410 methods that depend on libraries, fields and other methods, averaging 33.1 test cases per class.

entries.name: Aider polyglot benchmark
entries.summary: Programming exercises taken from Exercism's C++, Go, Java, JavaScript, Python and Rust tracks, used by Aider's benchmark harness; the exercises keep Exercism's licences.

entries.name: Commit0
entries.summary: Challenge to rebuild 57 core Python libraries from their specification and documentation until their unit tests pass, with tooling to run tests in isolated environments.

entries.name: FEA-Bench
entries.summary: Feature-implementation tasks built from pull requests in 83 GitHub repositories, each paired with unit test files that check the new code.

entries.name: SWT-Bench
entries.summary: Test-generation benchmark and harness: given a repository and an issue, write a test that fails on the original code and passes once the fix is applied.

entries.name: SWE-Bench Pro
entries.summary: 1,865 long-horizon problems from 41 repositories, split into a public set and held-out and commercial sets whose problems are not released.

entries.name: OpenHands (paper)
entries.summary: Describes the OpenHands platform, formerly OpenDevin, for agents that write code, use a command line and browse the web inside sandboxed environments, with built-in benchmarks.

entries.name: SWE-ReX
entries.summary: Runtime interface that lets agent code run shell sessions locally, in Docker containers or on remote machines with the same API, and run many sessions in parallel.

entries.name: Inspect
entries.summary: Python framework for language model evaluations with components for prompt engineering, tool use, multi-turn dialogue and model-graded scoring.

entries.name: Inspect Evals
entries.summary: Library of evaluations implemented on the Inspect framework, including ports of HumanEval, MBPP and SWE-bench, with a register for evaluations hosted elsewhere.

entries.name: Terminal-Bench 2.0
entries.summary: Second version of the Terminal-Bench task set, in which agents do work in containerised environments, run through the Harbor package.

entries.name: Benchmarks as Software
entries.summary: Argues that benchmarks accumulate maintenance debt as models and infrastructure change, and applies a continuous-validation workflow to Terminal-Bench 2.0.

entries.name: AppWorld
entries.summary: Environment of 9 everyday apps reachable through 457 APIs and filled with activity for about 100 fictitious people, plus 750 tasks solved by writing code and checked by state-based tests.

entries.name: MLE-bench
entries.summary: 75 machine learning engineering competitions from Kaggle with human baselines from the public leaderboards, used to measure agents that train models and run experiments.

entries.name: Cybench
entries.summary: Framework for specifying cybersecurity tasks for agents, with 40 Capture the Flag tasks from four competitions and subtasks for finer-grained scoring.

entries.name: Quantifying Variance in Evaluation Benchmarks
entries.summary: Measures how much benchmark scores move with training seed and over training, across many models, and gives recommendations for judging whether a difference is meaningful.

entries.name: Holistic Agent Leaderboard
entries.summary: Shared harness that runs agent evaluations in parallel across many VMs, used for 21,730 rollouts over 9 models and 9 benchmarks to compare models, scaffolds and benchmarks.

entries.name: Are "Solved Issues" in SWE-bench Really Solved Correctly?
entries.summary: Tests and inspects patches that pass SWE-bench Verified against the developers' patches, using a differential testing technique called PatchDiff, to count plausible but incorrect fixes.

entries.name: UTBoost
entries.summary: Generates extra unit tests for SWE-bench instances and finds 36 instances whose original tests were insufficient and 345 patches that had been wrongly counted as passing.

entries.name: Hack-Verifiable Terminal Bench
entries.summary: Embeds detectable hacks into Terminal-Bench tasks so that reward hacking can be counted automatically, and measures how prompting about the hack changes the rate.

entries.name: LessLeak-Bench
entries.summary: Study of data leakage across 83 software engineering benchmarks: average leakage ratios of 4.8%, 2.8% and 0.7% for Python, Java and C/C++, and far higher for a few such as QuixBugs.

entries.name: CodeContests
entries.summary: Competitive programming problems from Aizu, AtCoder, CodeChef, Codeforces and HackerEarth with input-output tests and correct and incorrect human solutions; non-code files are CC BY 4.0, and the repository is archived.

entries.name: AlphaCode (CodeContests paper)
entries.summary: Introduces the AlphaCode system and the CodeContests dataset, evaluated in simulated Codeforces contests by sampling many programs and filtering them by how they behave on example tests.

entries.name: bigcode-evaluation-harness
entries.summary: Framework that runs code generation models from the Hugging Face Hub on tasks such as HumanEval, MBPP, APPS and DS-1000 and scores them by executing the generated code.

entries.name: RepoCoder and RepoEval
entries.summary: Iterative retrieval and generation for repository-level code completion, with the RepoEval benchmark of line, API call and function body completions taken from recent real repositories.

entries.name: DevEval
entries.summary: 1,874 code generation samples from 117 real repositories in 10 domains, annotated by 13 developers with requirements, reference code and the dependencies each function uses.

entries.name: Multi-SWE-bench (paper)
entries.summary: Describes 1,632 annotated issue-resolution instances in seven languages besides Python, results for Agentless, SWE-agent and OpenHands, and 4,723 further instances released for reinforcement learning.

entries.name: SWE-bench-extra
entries.summary: Issue and pull request pairs from 1,988 Python repositories (6,415 in the card's text, 6,376 rows in its metadata) built with the SWE-bench method; the card names SWE-rebench as its successor.

entries.name: Gorilla and the Berkeley Function Calling Leaderboard (BFCL)
entries.summary: Repository holding the Gorilla API-calling models and the BFCL function-calling benchmark, whose later versions add multi-turn and multi-step calls and agentic tasks such as web search and memory.

entries.name: AI Agents That Matter
entries.summary: Argues that agent benchmarks should report cost alongside accuracy, separate the needs of model and application developers, keep proper held-out sets and standardise evaluation so results can be reproduced.

entries.name: Quantifying Contamination in Evaluating Code Generation Capabilities of Language Models
entries.summary: Measures surface-level and semantic overlap between popular code generation benchmarks and open training corpora, and finds models score better on problems whose similar solutions were seen in training.
